gen-gf-tuffy-fs-literata: Tuffy cuts every curve at a single depth, with endings that stay open to the light. Literata, a text serif, thickens gently at the shoulders and gives a page its bookish, sturdy texture.
gen-gf-uchen-fs-bespoke-sans: Dignified and mildly modulated, Uchen never pinches its letters shut. Bespoke Sans sits beneath it in a plain sans, sharp and spacious, so the serif's authority has a crisp, refined partner.
gen-gf-unna-fs-bespoke-sans: Bespoke Sans reads sharp and refined, with generous gaps where each curve meets its stem, so it can sit at modest sizes. Unna's pointed-nib swells supply the drama.
gen-gf-uoqmunthenkhung-fs-bespoke-sans: UoqMunThenKhung pairs hairline-fine thins with very heavy thicks, giving headings a classic, authoritative bite against its quieter partner. Shrink it, and those thins would nearly vanish.
gen-gf-urbanist-fs-literata: Clean and open, Urbanist draws every stroke without contrast. Literata, a text serif, does the opposite job: its sturdy thins and slightly heavier thicks give sentences a bookish, sophisticated warmth, where Urbanist keeps headings crisp.
gen-gf-varela-fs-literata: Wire-bent and rounded, Varela looks modern and inviting, its letters staying open throughout. Literata's gently modulated strokes would carry a long read with a bookish ease.
gen-gf-varela-round-fs-literata: Soft as thin plastic tubing bent into loops, Varela Round has no hairlines anywhere, and its curves stay open. Literata adds a restrained brush-like swell beneath.
gen-gf-varta-fs-literata: Friendly and modern, with a big visible entrance into each curved letter. Literata, the serif below, offers medium contrast without sharp hairlines, and that sturdy, bookish texture is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-gf-vazirmatn-fs-literata: Literata reads as bookish and sophisticated, with sturdy thins beside slightly heavier thicks. Vazirmatn handles headings best, with low contrast and open apertures, while the serif body's subtle weight change feels like etched lines in glass.
gen-gf-vibes-bitter: Huddled, bold and unshaded, Vibes packs its lowercase up toward the caps with no thick-to-thin shift at all. Bitter, a slab-serif, feels dependable and grounded beside it.
